The Nine-Card Convergence Atlas

Nine exemplar series sit side by side on a 3 by 3 grid, one card each.

Each card holds one partial-sum curve and one verdict line. Green converges, red diverges. Side by side, the differences show.

For example, spread nine 🗂️ cards on a desk. Series that looked alike one at a time show their forks clearly next to their neighbors.

Show the harmonic series diverges by grouping terms into blocks of powers of 222, and explain why terms going to 000 is not enough.

12k+1+⋯+12k+1≥2k⋅12k+1=12\frac{1}{2^k + 1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{2^{k+1}} \ge 2^k \cdot \frac{1}{2^{k+1}} = \frac122k+11​+⋯+2k+11​≥2k⋅2k+11​=21​
Show proof

  1. The block from 2k+12^k + 12k+1 to 2k+12^{k+1}2k+1 has 2k2^k2k terms, each at least 12k+1\frac{1}{2^{k+1}}2k+11​, so each block sums to at least 12\frac1221​.

  2. There are infinitely many blocks, so the partial sums pass every bound: the harmonic series diverges.

  3. The terms 1k\frac1kk1​ go to 000 yet the series diverges. Terms going to 000 is necessary for convergence, never sufficient, and this card is the counterexample.

Show the alternating harmonic series converges but does not converge absolutely.

∑k=1∞(−1)k+1k=ln⁡2,∑k=1∞∣(−1)k+1k∣=∑k=1∞1k=∞\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} = \ln 2, \qquad \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \left|\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}\right| = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac1k = \inftyk=1∑∞​k(−1)k+1​=ln2,k=1∑∞​​k(−1)k+1​​=k=1∑∞​k1​=∞
Show proof

  1. The terms 1k\frac1kk1​ decrease monotonically to 000, so the Leibniz test gives convergence. The even and odd partial sums can also be seen closing on one limit directly.

  2. Taking absolute values gives the harmonic series, which diverges. So the convergence is conditional only.

  3. The sum is ln⁡2\ln 2ln2, from the series for ln⁡(1+x)\ln(1 + x)ln(1+x) at x=1x = 1x=1, and the convergence is slow: the partial-sum error is of order 1n\frac{1}{n}n1​.
